overall: The Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by creating insufficiently detailed executive session minutes and by failing to timely respond to complaints; the notice and purpose claims were rejected and the records-request complaint was declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint 1 alleged the executive session notice and pre-session announcement did not sufficiently describe the purpose of the session.
allegations.key_passage: Where the notice and announcement identified the specific litigation matter to be discussed in executive session, we find that they were both sufficient.

allegations.summary: Complaints 1 and 3 alleged the Purpose 3 litigation executive session was improper because no litigation remained after the court ruling and the Order of Conditions was discussed.
allegations.key_passage: A discussion of whether to pursue an appeal is the type of strategic litigation decision protected by Purpose 3.

allegations.summary: Complaint 3 alleged the minutes of the November 30 executive session were insufficiently detailed to show what was discussed.
allegations.key_passage: Because the minutes of the November 30 executive session lack the requisite level of detail, we find that the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The Commission failed to respond to two complaints within 14 business days, and its response to the third came about seven weeks late.
allegations.key_passage: The Commission’s continued failure to comply with the requirement to review and respond to Open Meeting Law complaints within 14 business days is concerning and is itself a violation of the Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint 2 concerned a Public Records Law request for draft executive session minutes and did not clearly allege an Open Meeting Law violation.
allegations.key_passage: The second complaint arises out of a request the Complainant made under the Public Records Law for draft minutes of the November 30 executive session and does not clearly allege any violation of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Amend the November 30 executive session minutes to include a substantive summary of the discussions and release the amended minutes to the public, subject to appropriate redactions, within 30 days.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: we order the Commission, within 30 days of the date of this determination, to amend the minutes of its November 30 executive session to include a substantive summary of the discussions that were held and to release the amended minute to the public, subject to appropriate redactions.
